lesson.title: Pronoun Hook vs Left-Walk: lo quiero vs quiero verlo
lesson.subtitle: Why Spanish lets object pronouns either walk left of the conjugated verb (Lo quiero ver) or hook onto the tail of the infinitive (Quiero verlo, Voy a comprarlo)

hook.title: Two Legal Parking Spots for 'It'
hook.content: This is one of the most liberating rules in *Complete Spanish*. When you have ONE conjugated verb ('I want it'), the object pronoun has only one spot: right in front of the verb (Lo quiero). But when you have a TWO-VERB chain — like quiero ver ('I want to see'), voy a comprar ('I am going to buy'), or puedo confirmar ('I can confirm') — Spanish gives you a 100% free choice between TWO spots!

pattern.title: Option 1: Walk Before the First Verb — Option 2: Hook onto the Infinitive!
pattern.content:
Want to say 'I am going to buy it' (referring to el libro)?
• Spot 1 (Left-Walk): Lo voy a comprar.
• Spot 2 (Infinitive Hook): Voy a comprarlo.
Both are 100% natural, everyday Spanish with zero difference in meaning! The only forbidden spot is in the middle between the two verbs (*Voy a lo comprar is impossible).

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I am going to buy it (hooked)
I am going to buy it (left-walk)

exercises.target_answer: quiero verlo, lo quiero ver, voy a comprarlo, lo voy a comprar, puedo confirmarla
exercises.meaning: I want to see it (hooked), I want to see it (left-walk), I am going to buy it (hooked), I am going to buy it (left-walk), I can confirm it (feminine, hooked)
exercises.explanation: Before the conjugated verb (two words) or hooked onto the infinitive (one welded word) — never in between!

exercises.prompt: Hook 'la' ('it', feminine) onto the tail of 'preparar' to form 'to prepare it':
exercises.explanation: preparar + la welds into one word: prepararla.

exercises.prompt: Which of these three ways to say 'I am going to see it' is FORBIDDEN in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Unlike French (Je vais le voir), Spanish NEVER puts an object pronoun between the two verbs! Put it at the very front (Lo voy a ver) or welded to the tail (Voy a verlo).

exercises.prompt: Assemble using the Left-Walk position: 'I am going to buy it'
exercises.meaning: I am going to buy it
exercises.explanation: Lo + voy + a + comprar — pronoun walks in front of the whole verb chain.

exercises.idea: say 'I am going to see it today' by hooking 'lo' onto the end of 'ver'
cues: I am going to → Voy a
to see it (ver + lo welded) → verlo
idea_parts: I am going to → Voy a
exercises.meaning: I am going to see it today
exercises.explanation: Voy a verlo hoy — hooking onto the infinitive keeps the thought flowing in English-like order!

diagnosis.slip: wrote ver lo as two words
diagnosis.cue: When placed after an infinitive, the pronoun must attach as one single word: verlo.

summary.outcome: Place object pronouns either before the conjugated verb (Lo voy a ver) or welded onto the infinitive (Voy a verlo).

use_example.german: Voy a comprarlo hoy — sí, lo voy a comprar.
use_example.english: I am going to buy it today — yes, I am going to buy it.

summary.takeaway: Front of the train (Lo voy a ver) or hooked to the caboose (Voy a verlo) — never between the cars!
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([13] por vs para): master Spanish's two words for 'for' with the Arrow and the Scale.

twist.explanation: No puedo verlo (or No lo puedo ver).

lo.etymology_derivation: Latin illum → lo. Walks one step to the left of conjugated verbs: I it want.

la.etymology_derivation: Latin illa → la. It functions as both the feminine definite article ('the') and the direct object pronoun ('her / it').

ver.context_translation: I am going to see it/him today.
ver.etymology_derivation: Pronouns can hook directly onto the tail of the infinitive: verlo ('to see it/him')!

comprar.etymology_derivation: Latin comparāre ('to get ready, purchase') — English compare.

confirmar.etymology_derivation: confirmación → confirmar. Strip -ación, attach -ar. One rule turns hundreds of nouns into verbs.

preparar.context_translation: I want to prepare the coffee.
preparar.etymology_derivation: preparación → preparar. Latin praeparāre ('to make ready beforehand').

voy.context_translation: I am going to visit Madrid.
voy.etymology_derivation: Followed by a + infinitive, voy a expresses the near future.

querer.etymology_derivation: Latin quaerere ('to seek, ask for') evolved in Spanish to 'to want' and 'to love'. When you make an inquiry in English, you are asking what you want.

puedo.english_meaning: I can, I am able to
puedo.etymology_derivation: o splits into ue under stress.
